#4566. Tesla toughens FSD driver monitoring in Europe while loosening it in the US

Tesla is rolling out stricter driver monitoring for its “Full Self-Driving” system in Europe, with earlier warnings, a full strike for drivers who look away during a manoeuvre, and a hands-on-wheel requirement above 130 km/h (81 mph).

In the US, Tesla has spent the last year going the other way. Its CEO told owners they can text and drive on FSD, and recent US builds were tuned to nag drivers less.

On November 16, the Dutch vehicle authority RDW announced that it signed off on a new update to Tesla Assisted Driving, the name Tesla now uses for FSD (Supervised) in Europe. It covers HW4 vehicles and goes out over the air.

According to the RDW, drivers now get attention warnings earlier. If a driver isn’t paying attention while the system performs a manoeuvre, they get a “full strike.” The regulator says the update also adds measures to prevent misuse of the system, but it didn’t spell out what they are.

There’s a speed component too. Above 130 km/h (where legal), the driver has to keep their hands on the wheel. And setting a maximum speed above what the system displays now requires the driver to confirm it by scrolling the wheel up, with the speed limit sign pulsing red when the car goes over.

The RDW says it tested the update on its own track and on public roads and found no adverse or unintended effects. Ten other countries have adopted the Dutch approval so far, with Finland now on the list, while EU-wide approval is still waiting on a vote at the TCMV, the committee of member states.

This comes two weeks after Tesla cut the system’s speed margin from 50% to 10% over the limit in Europe and dropped the “Full Self-Driving” name there. Germany had made both a condition of supporting EU approval.

Now look at how Tesla handles the same software at home.

At Tesla’s shareholder meeting last November, Musk complained that the car was “a little strict about keeping your eyes on the road” and said Tesla would “allow you to text and drive essentially” within a month or two. A month later, an owner asked whether FSD v14.2.1 allowed texting. Musk’s answer: “Depending on context of surrounding traffic, yes.”

Texting while driving is illegal in 49 states. FSD is still a Level 2 system, and Tesla’s own fine print says the driver is responsible at all times.

In May, Musk confirmed that FSD v14.3.3 was built to nag drivers less. Tesla did add better eye-gaze tracking and eyewear handling in a June build, to be fair. But the pitch to owners hasn’t changed: fewer nags is sold as a feature.

And US drivers have been allowed to go hands-free on FSD at any speed since Tesla moved to cabin-camera monitoring in 2024. There’s no 130 km/h rule here.

NHTSA noticed. In its engineering analysis of FSD crashes in low-visibility conditions, the agency asked Tesla to justify a list of its marketing claims, and it specifically cited Musk’s texting post. In September, Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi asked NHTSA to look into Tesla’s driver monitoring after dozens of videos appeared to show drivers asleep on Autopilot and FSD.

The results are on the road. Last month, a driver told the CHP he was asleep on FSD when his Tesla drove through a freeway closure and hit a patrol car, seriously injuring two officers. Owners are also filming themselves defeating Tesla’s driver monitoring and posting it for clout.

Both markets get the same cabin camera and the same HW4 computer.

But in Europe, a type-approval authority tests every update before it ships and can refuse it. In the US, nobody pre-approves driver-assist software. Tesla self-certifies, and NHTSA only steps in after complaints and crashes pile up, which is how you end up with a CEO publicly telling owners to text while the regulator is still writing letters about it.

This update proves Tesla can build stricter driver monitoring whenever a regulator demands it. The code exists. It’s running on HW4 cars in 11 European countries right now.

That's because Musk is buddies with the current federal government that would regulate his not-full-self-driving system. Whereas Europe doesn't kowtow to his whims. We'll see what happens in 2029 with a new administration.

That makes the US approach hard to defend. Tesla’s argument for relaxing supervision is that FSD is now good enough. But if that were true, it would be showing the RDW data proving looser monitoring is safe, not adding earlier warnings and harsher strikes to get approved. It’s doing the opposite in Europe because it has to, and the opposite of that in the US because it can.

We’ve been saying it for a while: FSD gets more dangerous as it gets better, because people trust it more and watch the road less. The answer is monitoring that tightens as the system improves. Europe is forcing exactly that. In the US, Tesla is loosening it, encouraging illegal phone use from the top, and leaving drivers with 100% of the liability when it goes wrong.

So here’s the question for Tesla. If European owners are getting earlier warnings and instant strikes, why not American owners on the exact same software? Or is NHTSA going to have to force it?

#4565. Nearly 3 million pages of military records from the War of 1812 are finally online

Published Nov 19, 2026 2:01 PM EST

After 16 years of painstaking work, the National Archives and its collaborators have finally completed digitizing over 180,000 pension applications submitted to the United States government following the War of 1812. The project is more than just preservation for preservation’s sake. The roughly 2.8 million pages contain long-forgotten and missing details about 19th century Americans, their families, and their everyday lives.

While archivists previously digitized a similar collection related to the American Revolutionary War, the new documents will help fill in knowledge gaps between early 19th century military events and the 1850 federal census. Patricia Oxley, president of the Federation of Genealogical Societies (FGS), explained the project was also incredibly time-sensitive.

“In the specific case of the War of 1812 pension records, there is an added priority due to their frail state where not acting may mean sacrificing these for future generations,” Oxley said in a recent announcement.

The somewhat new United States of America declared war on the United Kingdom on June 18, 1812, citing objections to trade restrictions with France amid the Napoleonic Wars, as well as the Royal Navy’s impressment of American sailors. Although the conflict famously included a British attack on Washington D.C. that resulted in the burning of the White House and U.S. Capitol, little shifted geopolitically between the two nations following the ratification of the Treaty of Ghent on February 17, 1815. The U.S. tallied around 15,000 casualties, while the U.K. and Canada saw about 10,700 deaths. Another 9,000 Indigenous fighters died while enlisted between the two sides.

Today’s military records are meticulously documented and stored digitally, but applying for benefits such as pensions was a much more labor-intensive process during the 19th century. With the burden of proof on each applicant, veterans were required to supply lengthy accounts of their service. Each War of 1812 pension file is liable to contain not just combat information, but the names and personal details of fellow soldiers, family members, spouses, and countless other relations.

“Our users have been asking for the War of 1812 pension records for some time, and I expect this collection to be very popular based on the rich war time detail it contains,” added Brian Hansen, general manager at Fold3, Ancestry’s military records service and National Archives collaborator.

The collection also includes a full-text search feature using handwriting recognition technology. This lets users explore the files based on every named individual, and not simply the primary veteran applicants. The pension records are currently available for free on Fold3’s website, and are being added to the National Archives catalog on a rolling basis.

Correction 11/20/26 9:30 a.m. EST: A previous version of this article incorrectly stated the pension archive contained around 7 million files. This was based on an initial assessment from researchers in 2010. The article has been updated to reflect the more accurate tally.

#4564. The Vintage Modern Fastback Is the Anti-Restomod Mustang

Take one S650-gen Mustang GT; add 900 hours of labor and carbon-fiber body parts; serve with 840 hp.

Taking a vintage muscle car and swapping in modern components to make it run better or add power is a story as old as, well, the LS2 V-8. Vintage Modern’s new Fastback Mustang turns that formula upside down—by swapping old-school body parts onto a modern S650-generation Mustang GT. But the Vintage Modern Fastback, officially revealed on Wednesday at Retromobile New York, is more than just a body kit.

For starters, Ford’s standard 5.0-liter V-8 is mated here to a 3.0-liter Whipple supercharger for a total output of 840 horsepower and 615 lb-ft of torque. Prospective buyers can choose between a six-speed manual transmission with rev matching or a 10-speed automatic with steering-wheel-mounted paddle shifters. Other high-end Mustang features like active-valve performance exhaust with four sound modes, MagneRide adaptive suspension, six selectable drive modes, and Brembo performance brakes are also standard fare.

“The Vintage Fastback is a car we’ve always wanted to build. We’ve blended classic-inspired design with modern safety, technology, and performance,” said Chau Nguyen, founder and CEO of Vintage Modern. “This is what Vintage Modern was created to do.”

Even though the bones of the Fastback are from a current-generation Mustang, the heavily modified vehicle still underwent crash testing to meet applicable Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards. This retro-inspired Mustang features eight airbags, crumple zones, side-impact beams, electronic stability control, traction control, and anti-lock brakes. That’s more than most restomod Mustang owners can say.

Most of the custom body panels, including the functional hood scoop, are carbon fiber; the only obviously metal pieces are the billet-aluminum grille, door handles, mirrors, and twin auxiliary driving lights. Similarly, the interior of the retro Fastback build features Alcantara and billet-aluminum trim over three different seat upholsteries: pleated, diamond-quilted, or woven. Each buyer can choose from more than 40 standard paint colors, as well as paint-to-sample finishes and stripe options, along with their own interior configurations; Vintage Modern is also offering an optional JL Audio premium sound system and leather-trimmed floor mats.

Vintage Modern’s carbon-fiber body panels are hand-made in Detroit before being assembled and finished at its Atlanta facility; all told, each unit requires around 900 hours of hands-on labor. The builder has big plans, too; it says it has plans to move into a new factory three times the size of its existing facility, hire more than 100 additional team members, and triple production capacity within two years.

No pricing details about the Vintage Modern Fastback were available at the time of publication, but we’ll update this story when we learn more.

#4563. Kia went from this one quirky EV 40 years ago to an entire electric lineup

The Kia Besta EV hit the roads in 1986 as the brand’s first fully electric vehicle. 40 years later, Kia continues to “lead the pack” with a full lineup of EVs ranging from entry-level cars and SUVs to three-row models, and just about everything in between.

Kia wanted to design a new vehicle for the 1986 Asian Games, which were held in Seoul, South Korea, one that did not emit any toxic fumes in front of runners.

So, it created the Besta EV. The Besta van was initially developed 40 years ago by Kia’s Central Research Institute as the successor to the popular Bongo van, which is still sold in Korea and other markets today.

Unlike the Bongo, it was developed using Kia’s in-house tech rather than sourced from another automaker and rebadged as its own.

Kia swapped the 2.0L four-cylinder diesel engine for a 35 kWh battery and electric motor, which provided a range of more than 26 miles (42 km) on a single charge.

While the Besta EV was never actually sold to the public, it laid the groundwork and offered an early glimpse at Kia’s shift to electrification.

The first mass-produced Korean EV certified for commercial sale was the Kia Pride EV in 1993. In 2011, the Ray EV became Kia’s first series-production electric car.

Kia expanded its electrification ambitions to Europe and the UK in 2014 with the first-generation Soul EV, the beloved boxy, funky crossover that was discontinued after the 2025 model year.

The Korean automaker has come a long way since the Besta EV, with a full lineup of electric vehicles ranging from compact cars to mid-size and three-row SUVs, vans, and just about everything in between.

Kia now offers an electric option for nearly everyone with seven-passenger EVs on sale in the UK and Europe, including the EV2, EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6, EV9, and PV5 Passenger van.

With its first software-defined vehicle (SDV) and a new B-segment electric hatchback set to launch by the end of 2027, Kia has no plans to slow down. On top of this, Kia will expand its PBV lineup with the PV7 next year, a larger sibling to the PV5.

Four decades after the Besta EV arrived, Kia said it continues to “lead the pack today” with one of the most diverse all-electric EV lineups of any brand.

Through October, Kia has sold over 135,000 EVs in the UK, with fully electric vehicles now accounting for over 37% of total sales.

Thanks to its new EV lineup, Kia became “Europe’s fastest-growing top 10 passenger-car brand.” According to the European Automobile Manufacturers’ Association, Kia registered 377,078 vehicles between January and August 2026, up 9% compared to the same period last year.

Sjoerd Knipping, Chief Operating Officer of Kia Europe, said the growth is thanks to having “one of the broadest and most advanced electrified line-ups in Europe.”

In the US, Kia launched the compact EV3 (check out our review of it) this year, starting at just $29,890. It joins the EV6, EV9, and Niro EV in Kia’s US electric vehicle lineup.

#4562. Where is bald eagle Kaydee? Shadow’s pal has avoided the nest.

Published Nov 19, 2026 2:13 PM EST

Turn off reality TV and turn on the bald eagle cams. It’s all the drama you need.

When internet-famous bald eagle Shadow seemingly welcomed a mysterious new female into his nest earlier this week, many fans have questioned the whereabouts of Kaydee. After the death of Shadow’s longtime partner Jackie in August, he had been spotted spending time with the 4-year-old banded female eagle named KD1 (later renamed Kaydee). It seemed like the eagles might head into mating season as a pair, but after the arrival of a new, large female, it’s unclear how the relationships will all shake out.

Since the appearance of the mystery female, nicknamed Big Beautiful Visitor or BBV by some fans, Kaydee has disappeared from view of Friends of Big Bear Valley (FOBBV)’s two cameras. She was last spotted by the cameras on November 14 in the Roost Tree, according to FOBBV. Despite concerns that she may be injured or had left the area, wildlife photographers have continued to document Kaydee’s presence near Big Bear Lake as recently as November 18.

Photographer Alla Shumko shared photos of Kaydee perched near Big Bear Lake on November 18. Kaydee’s double bands are visible as she observed a scuffle between younger eagles fighting over fish.

Mating season is well underway, so viewers of FOBBV’s 24/7 livecams have been watching closely for signs that Shadow has selected a new partner. Shadow has worked with both Kaydee and the new eagle on nest maintenance and shared “beaky kisses” with each female, both signs of bonding in bald eagles. Bald eagle mating involves a bit of aerial acrobatics—copulating pairs can be seen in what’s called a “cartwheel display,” in which they lock talons in mid-air while tumbling down to the ground. Male eagles do not have an external phallus, so mating occurs via a touch of cloacas. Vocalizations can typically be heard during the act, which lasts about 7 to 12 seconds, according to Raptor Resource.

As this is nature, we humans can’t predict or influence who Shadow will pick as a new partner. Or if he picks at all. All we can do is watch and wait and let nature take its course.

#4561. Lamborghini Temerario Spyder Delivers Open-Air Access to Its 10,000-RPM V-8

It’s the first power folding hardtop for a car from Sant'Agata Bolognese.

Lamborghini has its product development schedule finely tuned. Of course, there was a convertible version of the Temerario coming. And on Wednesday, November 18, the automaker unveiled it for the first time—and it is called, of course, the Temerario Spyder.

Formally introduced Thursday morning at the Academy Museum or Motion Pictures in Los Angeles, the Temerario Spyder isn’t surprising, but it’s still stunning. The Temerario was designed with the Spyder always in mind; as such, there’s space enough behind the two seats for the new power folding hardtop to snick down inside almost perfectly vertically. The firewall between the cockpit and the mid-mounted, twin-turbocharged V-8 doesn’t change its location, but the space behind the seats is utilized differently.

The folding solid top itself was co-developed by Germany’s Webasto, the venerable firm that’s also behind folding top modules from the Mazda MX-5 Miata RF to the Ferrari California. This is the first Lambo to use a retractable hardtop.

10 electric actuators split the two-piece top, open a hatch behind the seats, and move the structure down into its narrow warren. It’s a fully electric system, so there are no hydraulic lines to split open. Lamborghini says the power top adds about 100 kilograms (220 pounds) to the Temerario’s mass, but that’s all at the center of the car, so that front-to-rear weight balance is maintained. With the roof open, says the maker, the center of gravity drops about three millimeters from where it is when closed.

The hardtop should also produce close to a coupe-like experience when it is closed.“We reinforce the structure of the Spyder,” explains Fermin Soneira, Lambo’s chief technical officer, about the Temerario Spyder’s aluminum space frame. “So, for example, we use some hydroformed pieces in place of castings at some points.”

The Temerario Spyder takes the market position that was once held by the Huracan Spyder, and Lamborghini claims this new architecture is six percent stiffer in torsional rigidity and nine percent up in dynamic bending stiffness than that car. If all that stiff isn’t stiffy enough, there’s also a six percent increase in dynamic torsional rigidity. So, it’s a super-stiffy thing.

The increase in weight means the suspension has been slightly tweaked to deal with it. “If you change the weight, you have to change the spring rate to keep the same natural frequency,” says Soneira. “In this case, it was not about leaving everything the same, but also about increasing comfort in the ‘Strada’ drive mode. Still, if you go to the Hockenheimring, there’s less than a one second per lap difference between the coupe and the Spyder.”

Top up or down, the most spectacular element of every Temerario is the flat-plane crank, 4.0-liter twin-turbo V-8 that’s incorporated into the hybrid all-wheel drive powertrain. With a lightweight reciprocating assembly that includes titanium connecting rods, the engine will spin to a thrilling 10,000-rpm redline. “We have a new calibration of the engine sound,” adds Soneira, “so you end up with a slightly different voice than in the coupe. The target is always ‘let’s keep improving,’ so these changes will come to the coupe too.”

Combined with three electric motors, the Temerario has 907 horsepower aboard—and despite all the electronic hickey-doos, it still stirs up and blasts like a true supercar. That’s not likely to change with the Spyder.

Production of the Spyder will be done in batches along the regular Temerario assembly line, with the first saleable models due to be completed as this is published. Lamborghini expects about 50 percent of Temerario production to be Spyders. Prices haven’t been announced, but should start around $400,000 and go up from there only limited by the buyer’s imagination and wallet.

#4559. North Atlantic right whales named after Dolly Parton and Gonzo

Published Nov 19, 2026 3:00 PM EST

Less than 400 adult North Atlantic right whales (Eubalaena glacialis) still exist in the wild, making them one of the world’s most critically endangered species. Of those, 20 have officially received spiffy new names from conservationists at the New England Aquarium’s Anderson Cabot Center for Ocean Life. The researchers curate the annual North Atlantic Right Whale Catalog, and attach personable monikers to a select few baleen cetaceans in order to more easily monitor them. This year, it’s time to wave hello to Dodo, Volcano, and Dolly.

“Naming right whales is a fun and creative activity for our research community, but it also allows an opportunity to connect with the whales on an individual level,” Amy Warren, an aquarium scientific program officer and name project coordinator, said in Anderson Cabot Center’s announcement. “It can be hard to relate to Catalog #5299, but a whale named Nibbles is bound to be memorable.”

The 2026 inductees also include Grand Slam (Catalog #3991) and Slide (Catalog #4991). The sister whales have a mother named Fenway (Catalog #2791), who was also named in honor of the Boston Red Sox. Grand Slam earned her new name thanks to her three patches of raised tissue known as callosities that resemble the bases on a baseball field. Meanwhile, Slide received their name due to the curved scar on her back that recalls someone sliding through home plate. Other right whale names this year include Goose, Donegal, and even Gonzo for the beloved Muppet.

“Although the names are intended to help researchers at sea, they also give the general public a better understanding of the individual whales,” added Caroline Mowdy, a spokesperson for Whale and Dolphin Conservation (WDC).

Collaborators at the WDC also created some lighthearted, yearbook-esque biographies for each whale. For example, Dolly (Catalog #4191), whose callosity looks strikingly similar to the late, great country singer’s larger-than-life hair, apparently loves the song, “Jolene.” Then again, who doesn’t?

“We see these whales and their families grow each year,” said Mowdy. “Knowing them makes the tragedies even more tragic, but it also makes our determination to protect them even stronger.”

On Monday, the North Atlantic Right Whale Consortium announced that there are roughly 382 North Atlantic right whales, representing a 1.8 percent drop in population size from the 2024 estimate. Their primary threats remain getting tangled in fishing line and vessel strikes.

However, even amid their struggles, the 2025–2026 right whale calving season saw the most calves born since 2009. A total of 24 calves were born, including a surprising late addition that was spotted in Canada in September.

Expect 16 percent more horsepower than the regular four-cylinder G80, along with 30 percent better gas mileage.

Genesis just added a new member to its growing family. the 2028 Genesis G80 Hybrid. It’s Genesis’s second-ever hybrid, to be precise—and the G80 Hybrid, along with the related GV80 Hybrid, will showcase the first Hyundai Motor Group (HMG) hybrid system with a liquid-cooled battery.

Hyundai debuted its new liquid-cooled hybrid battery at a preview event on Tuesday, November 17, in Los Angeles, offering the media the chance to understand what makes it notable. By outperforming air-cooled systems with regard to temperature management, it unlocks higher peak discharge output and taps into more of the battery’s available power. Genesis first revealed its next-generation 2.5 Turbo Hybrid System for the GV80 Hybrid a few months ago, and now, we’re getting more details about how the same system will perform under the hood of the G80 Hybrid.

The electric-assisted 2.5-liter turbocharged inline-four produces a hearty 347 horsepower—16 percent more than the standard four-cylinder G80 model—and 391 pound-feet of torque. The engine will be mated to a seven-speed automatic transmission, with a choice of “manual” or “smart” adjustable regenerative braking settings; the smart setting will automatically adjust regenerative braking levels based on navigation information and traffic conditions. The G80 Hybrid will come in rear-wheel drive.

Genesis claims the G80 Hybrid will feature 30-percent improved fuel economy over a comparable G80 model with 19-inch wheels, with driving range estimates extending to over 500 miles. Since these claims are based on internal testing, we’ll have to wait to see what final EPA fuel economy and driving range estimates are.

Want to be able to spot a G80 Hybrid in the wild? There are a few small changes to the exterior that should help you spot one. There’s a redesigned 3-D grille, new 18- and 20-inch wheel designs, and a range of new exterior colors; you can choose from Wadden Gray, Milos Blue, and Barolo Red. If you want to stand out from other G80 Hybrid models, a Prestige Black variant will be available with a blacked-out exterior and interior, plus exclusive Black Ash Wood and alloy wheels.

Inside, the G80 Hybrid is identical to the standard G80, with Nappa leather seating surfaces and distinct quilting patterns on different trim levels. You’ll also find the Genesis-familiar 27-inch OLED integrated instrument cluster and navigation display, as well as the comprehensive suite of advanced driver assistance technologies the brand bakes into its new models.

Genesis has yet to announce pricing details or a production date for the 2028 G80 Hybrid, but it seems likely they’ll start to reach dealers sometime in late 2027. Interested in seeing the Genesis G80 Hybrid and GV80 Hybrid yourself before then? It will be displayed at the 2026 LA Auto Show during its public days, which run from November 20–29.

#4557. IONNA enables Plug & Charge for Tesla, opens 22 bay site in Westminster, CA

IONNA, the DC charging operator backed by several major OEMs, has opened its largest DC charging site yet, with 22 bays of 400kW charging in Westminster, California.

Alongside the opening, IONNA is also enabling Plug & Charge operation for Tesla EVs, with Stellantis EVs “coming soon.”

IONNA is a rapidly expanding DC charging network which is garnering good reviews from EV drivers, with clean, fast and easy to use charging stations (which it calls “Rechargeries”).

But until now, we haven’t had all that many chargers in the LA area. There are a couple in South OC and the Inland Empire, but nothing closer to the population center of the metro area (though more are opening soon).

That changes now with IONNA’s new flagship charging station in Westminster. It features 12 CCS connectors and 10 NACS ports, so you can charge just about any EV (no Chademo, nor can my AC-only Tesla Roadster charge here… ho hum).

In addition to 22 chargers with peak 400kW capacity, the site features indoor and outdoor lounge space, restrooms, and other amenities like an In N Out and a taco shop across the street. (Not quite as full-featured as my favorite charging station, Rove, but IONNA has a much larger national footprint, and does have faster chargers)

There’s also a small, convenience-store-like area that uses Amazon’s “just walk out” technology. You swipe a card to unlock the room, pick up any items you want, and just walk out. The many cameras on the ceiling track you (and whoever came in with you) and what you’re picking up, then charge your card for the items you took with you.

The store has snacks and drinks, though no ice cream, which is the main thing I’m looking for on a roadtrip stop… IONNA may convert one of the fridges to a freezer in the future, depending on how things go.

And, importantly, the site has trash cans and window wipers – just what you need on a roadtrip stop.

Speaking of roadtrips, the charger opening caps off a cross-country roadtrip by IONNA personnel, who set out in several cars from various parts of the country, all convening on the new Rechargery in Westminster.

Over 20 EVs joined the roadtrip and drove over 40,000 combined miles on their trip to Westminster. The teams charged at approximately 30% of the company’s charging sites, showing just how easy it is to do roadtrips in an EV.

The Rechargery opens tomorrow in Westminster, at 6260 Westminster Blvd, just off the 405 freeway. Look for the big sign. For the first weeks, you can charge at a promotional rate of $0.20/kWh. Afterwards, IONNA will charge its standard rate of $0.39/kWh.

Perhaps more importantly than a new charger opening, though, is IONNA’s announcement today that Teslas can now use its network with Plug & Charge functionality (well, technically Autocharge, which is basically the same thing).

Window wipers and fluid are an underrated missing feature at EV stations, hope to see more of this.

What this means is that you can link your car and credit card ahead of time (via the Presto charging app), then simply plug in at any IONNA station and start charging, without having to tap or swipe or open an app. This is similar to the experience Teslas have always had on Superchargers, so should be familiar to Tesla owners.

The functionality is rolled out across all of IONNA’s network, starting today. So you should be able to test it out on your Tesla vehicle. IONNA already supports Plug & Charge for BMW, GM, Hyundai, Kia, Mercedes-Benz, Toyota, Rivian, Ford, Porsche and Volvo EVs.

Further, IONNA says support is “coming soon” for Stellantis EVs (Jeep, Dodge, Ram, Fiat), stating that those cars will be able to Plug & Charge on its network in December. It now supports Autocharge for about two thirds of the EVs on American roads.

#4554. ‘We’re Moving Really Fast’: Ionna CEO On 500 kW EV Chargers And Flagship New Location

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Ionna, the electric vehicle charging consortium backed by major U.S. automakers including General Motors and Toyota, is growing its footprint in the U.S. at an astonishing pace.

In just over two years after the company was founded, it already has 224 operational sites across dozens of states. Now, it’s announcing a new flagship location, better access for the growing pool of Tesla drivers, more powerful stations, and discounted charging rates for Jeep, Dodge, and Fiat EV drivers.

The company on Wednesday opened its largest and fanciest charging location in the U.S., in Westminster, California. The new Rechargery has 22 stalls and is full of amenities.

It has canopies over the charging bays, outdoor seating, and a dedicated driver lounge. That's not it. You also get an arcade machine and round the clock access to Wi-Fi, coffee machine, and restrooms.

Seth Cutler, the CEO of Ionna, told InsideEVs in an interview that the company partnered with Amazon to build a 900-square-foot convenience store at the location which features the e-commerce giant’s Just Walk Out technology.

It lets customers tap their card while entering and directly walk out after shopping without having to stand in line or physically pay through a payment terminal.

“We're moving really fast to build this network up and provide a differentiated experience for customers,” Cutler said.

He added that multiple EVs can simultaneously charge at their maximum speeds at this station. Because it is backed by a whopping 4 megawatts of grid power, there are practically no power constraints for every day EV drivers.

“You could have 10 Lucid Gravitys and they can all pull 400 kilowatts,” Cutler said. “There’s only load management at the charger level,” he added.

That charger-level limit comes from how the hardware is set up. Each Ionna charging tower can deliver up to 400 kW, and each tower has two cables serving two parking spots.

If only one car is plugged in, the charger can dispense the full 400 kW, as long as the car can accept that speed. If two cars are plugged into the same tower, they share that 400 kW between them. The towers don’t draw from each other, so one busy tower never slows down the one next to it.

That means drivers can get back quickly on the road and the chance of long queues building up are less. In other words, you spend more time driving and less time charging.

The company is also preparing for future EVs that push the boundaries of ultra-fast charging speeds, at least for non-Chinese automakers.

Cutler said groundwork had already started to build 500-kilowatt stations in the U.S. Its current network comprises 400 kW-capable Alpitronic Hyperchargers, which are plenty quick by their own right.

He didn’t say when and where exactly these new chargers will open, but he added that the probable timeline is 2028 when more EVs on the market will actually be able to benefit from such high charging speeds.

Only a handful of EVs in the U.S. can currently accept even 400 kilowatts, let alone 500 kW. The Lucid Gravity, Porsche Cayenne Electric, and the BMW iX3 are capable of accepting 400 kW.

The upcoming Mercedes AMG GT will be able to charge at 600 kW when deliveries start next year. Owners have reported the Tesla Cybertruck pulling 500 kW for a brief window at the newer V4 Superchargers capable of dispensing such speeds.

That said, Tesla drivers can now get auto charge at Ionna stations using fleet charging company Presto's app. Plug & Charge is already enabled at Ionna for BMW, General Motors, Toyota, Volvo, Rivian, Ford, Hyundai, Kia, Mercedes-Benz, Porsche, and Volvo.

Downloading another smartphone app, however, might be unnecessary for Tesla drivers who already use the ubiquitous Supercharger network.

Starting in December, Ionna is also offering a 10% discount for EVs under the Stellantis umbrella. So drivers with the Jeep Wagoneer S, Dodge Charger Daytona, and the Fiat 500e will benefit from lower charging rates. If they have a connected services subscription, they get an additional 15% discount at Ionna taking the total to 25%.

And finally, Ionna’s network is now dense enough for coast-to-coast road trips just using Ionna charging stations. That’s something the company demonstrated this week with multiple drivers that set-off from New York, Raleigh, and Miami among other cities in a journey that culminated in California.

It’s a big achievement that proves that even though EV sales are up and down, the country’s charging network is growing quickly and is now better than ever.

#4553. Genesis Is Trying to Bring Its 1100-HP X-Scorpio SUV Concept to Production, Hyundai CEO Says

Jose Muñoz says feedback to the wild off-roader was so strong, the carmaker has to take a stab at bringing it to showrooms.

Genesis might be a carmaker that has so far largely stuck to meat-and-potatoes models like sedans and SUVs, but the Korean luxury brand has also pumped out quite a few tantalizing concept cars in recent years. Some of them, like the G90 Wingback and Magma GT supercar, have seemed almost production-ready; others, like the X Gran Equator and X-Scorpio off-roaders, less so. But according to Automotive News, the wild X-Scorpio concept could in fact wind up in showrooms—and none other than Hyundai CEO Jose Muñoz is the one spreading the news.

“We are working with designers to try to put [the X-Scorpio] into the market,” Muñoz told AN. The feedback that Genesis received from dealers and potential customers was so positive, he said, that “we are going to give it a try.”

If the X-Scorpio does reach showrooms, it would mark yet another flank in the Hyundai Motor Group’s fast-moving and wide-ranging onslaught of off-road trucks and SUVs. Hyundai and Kia have both made clear plans for multiple body-on-frame vehicles, including ones inspired by the Hyundai Boulder concept revealed at this year’s New York Auto Show; Genesis itself, meanwhile, has confirmed the luxurious X Gran Equator will enter production, potentially rivaling everything from the Lexus LX to the Mercedes-Benz G-wagen.

Still, none of those are anything like the X-Scorpio. In fact, there’s nothing quite like it on sale today, period. The concept, at least, is something of a cross between a Local Motors Rally Fighter and a Lamborghini Huracan Sterrato, with a twin-turbo V-8 putting out 1100 horsepower and 850 pound-feet of torque that gets sent to 40-inch off-road tires on 18-inch beadlock wheels. It was designed, the company says, for the Middle East, where screaming across open terrain and sending it off sand dunes is, as the press release politely puts it, “a favorite pastime”—but considering how those are also quite popular here in the United States (see: TRX, Ram; Raptor, Ford), it seems likely a production X-Scorpio would also be a hit here.

Of course, talk is cheap, even if it’s an automotive CEO saying it. Genesis does indeed have big plans for a bunch of new cars over the next few years, with 22 all-new or revised models coming by 2030. But whether there’s room on the balance sheet to develop for a bespoke off-road sports car with no direct competitors seems like a fairly large question mark, so let’s just keep our fingers crossed for now.

#4551. This GM EV1 Lives After A Painstaking Restoration

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

When this GM EV1 project car finally drove into daylight, it was 30 years to the day from when the very first EV1 rolled off the assembly line. Nicknamed V212, after a part of its VIN that proves it's the 212th EV1 ever made, the plucky little electric hatchback is finally back on the road after a nearly 20 year hiatus, much of that spent in a Georgia impound lot. Rebuilding this three-decade-old EV was no easy task but with a bunch of help, even some from GM itself, the EV1 is alive once again.

Watching V212 roll out of the garage was a moment 12 months in the making. It all started at the Georgia impound lot, where the V212 sold for $104,000, despite being sun-faded, tired, and legally abandoned. The forgotten EV1 was bought by Apple employee Billy Caruso, who owns several early EVs, and the restoration was done by Caruso, Jared Pink from The Questionable Garage, and GM. Engineers and designers from GM who worked on the EV1 back in the day helped support the project and offered up parts from an old donor car.

Caruso brought the V212 to Kettering University in Flint, Michigan, to celebrate its finished restoration, where he interviewed some of the people who worked on the original EV1 project. And the passion and love that everyone who worked on the EV1 has is evident. The EV1 wasn't the most successful car GM ever made, but it was a massively important project for the future of the brand and one that made a massive impact on everyone involved.

"Honestly, I've had a lot of really good roles in my career," said Linda Ludek Brouns, former propulsion system engineer for EV1. "Hands-down favorite was my time working on EV1.

Caruso's project wasn't an easy one. V212 received a full strip-down to bare metal, its interior was completely removed, and even its glass came out. Its interior was refreshed, it received all new glass, and it was painted. It was a painstaking process but V212 now is about as fresh as it was in 1996.

Bringing cars back to life is always heartwarming for us gearheads. But when that car is as rare and special as the EV1, it's so much more meaningful. The story is made even more special by Caruso being able to show it off to the people who designed, engineered, and built it. Thankfully, due to Caruso being willing to spend six figures on a project car, The Questionable Garage's dedication to the project, and GM's help, a piece of automotive history lives on instead of wasting away in the Georgia sun.

#4550. New electric comb from China regrew nearly 100% of hair (in mice)

Published Nov 19, 2026 4:10 PM EST

A potentially revolutionary electronic comb is generating some pretty hair-raising results. The experimental comb has been used to successfully restore nearly all the hair in bald test subjects. But don’t chuck out that Rogaine just yet. The comb’s users were mice with shaved backs.

Though the Detangle comb (named after the 2010 Disney film Tangled) hasn’t been tested on humans yet, the Chinese scientist behind its development says the eye-grabbing results on our distant genetic cousins suggest it could play a role in the neverending quest to keep those luscious locks just a hair longer.

Created by a team led by Beihang University in Beijing, the comb initially looks like the chunky plastic kind adorning typical pharmacy aisles. However, a closer look at its clear plastic handle reveals a green circuit board. Further down, one can see electrodes embedded in the comb’s teeth, which alternate between long and short. The team says that this height variance makes the comb’s pulsed electric field more than two and a half times stronger than it would be with evenly matched teeth.

The shorter teeth also contain two experimental genetic treatments. One boosts blood vessel growth around the hair follicles. The other treatment  blocks dihydrotestosterone (DHT), a hormone known to shrink follicles. The electric field generated by the comb temporarily opens up skin so the treatments can get inside, reaching up to nine times deeper into the follicle region than a conventional cream.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

Researchers performed a variety of tests on mice that had their backs shaved and were given testosterone to mimic pattern baldness. Over 28 days, the balding mice were treated with minoxidil or finasteride (the current standards for medical hair restoration), the comb’s electrical stimulation alone, and the comb combined with an experimental genetic treatment. Mice given finasteride regrew about 50 percent of their hair, while the ones on and minoxidil regrew 70 percent. Those numbers  honestly aren’t  too bad on their own, but the results were even better when Detangle got involved. Mice treated with the comb and both experimental treatments saw a staggering 97.85 percent hair regrowth. And all without having to book a flight to Turkey for a hair transplant.

“[T]hese results demonstrate that electrostimulation via the Detangle system promotes hair growth and follicle regeneration in a safe and effective manner,” the team wrote in their paper published earlier this month in the Nature Communications.

The potential market for a hair regrowing comb is sizable to say the least. Detangle’’s creators say androgenetic alopecia, the scientific term for pattern baldness, affects 1.5 billion people worldwide. Some studies suggest up to 80 percent of men will experience pattern baldness, with  some populations seeing symptoms before the age of 40. Somewhere between one fifth and two fifths of women may also experience pattern hair thinning. And hair isn’t just hair. Social expectations and norms around hair partly explain why hair loss can carry psychological baggage.

Scientists and hair care providers know this, of course. Toupees, tonics, and tinctures promising to reverse nature’s balding date back thousands of years. Today, the standard medical treatment usually involves topical minoxidil (the active ingredient in Rogaine) and oral finasteride. Minoxidil generally works, but results vary widely from person to person and it requires constant, ongoing application.

Finasteride is often far more effective, with long-term studies showing it can preserve hair in most men for at least a decade, but it also carries the risk for much more intense side effects. The drug (which saw a surge in popularity thanks to online, telehealth services) has been linked to decreased libido and erectile dysfunction. Some patients have also reported anxiety, depression, and suicidal thoughts. While the side effects are uncommon, the risk presented a potentially steep trade off for a fuller head of hair.

Those intrigued by the comb will unfortunately have to hold out quite a bit longer. The team says more research is needed before the device is tested on humans and, even then, there’s no guarantee the rodent results will translate. Testosterone-induced hair loss on a shaved mouse back is a far cry from human pattern baldness, which typically creeps in over years.

It’s also worth emphasizing that the electric comb, memorable as it is, wasn’t solely responsible for the best results. The pair of experimental genetic treatments used in the study (called SRD5A2 siRNA and VEGFA plasmids) also need to be tested in humans to ensure they are safe and don’t come with unintended side effects of their own. Wig stores, it seems, will live to see another day.

Toyota is recalling 19,000 electric C-HR SUVs globally, with about 10,000 affected in the US.

In September, Toyota issued a safety recall involving certain model-year 2026 C-HR electric SUVs in North America.

Toyota initially said about 10,000 models were involved, but later confirmed the number was 8,521 in a letter to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).

According to Germany’s federal motor authority, Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA), the recall has now expanded to 19,000 C-HR vehicles globally. In Germany, the recall impacts 1,096 vehicles and is still under investigation by the KBA.

The issue stems from faulty software programming in the EV-ECU. While it’s intended to limit the battery’s charge level, the software can cause it to overcharge under certain conditions.

Toyota said the issue occurs if the battery is already at a high state of charge and the driver continues using the regenerative braking system.

When this happens, warning lights and a sound will alert the driver, and the electric drive system can shut down, causing the vehicle to lose power while driving.

Following an internal investigation, Toyota said in the NHTSA report that the issue was caused by incorrect software that disrupted the charging-limit function, allowing the battery to overcharge while driving.

The Toyota C-HR vehicles included in the recall were produced between June 17, 2025, and July 9, 2026.

In Europe and other overseas markets, Toyota sells the C-HR EV as the C-HR+ to distinguish it from the gas- or hybrid-powered version.

OTA would be great, but there are some systems that are isolated and can't be updated that way. The EV-ECU is a core function system that is very likely sealed to prevent tampering. They never expected to need to reprogram it. It's like the firmware on your phone.

Owners of affected vehicles in North America can take them to a Toyota dealership, where the battery ECU software will be updated free of charge.

Toyota mailed owner notification letters out on October 18, 2026. Owners can contact Toyota’s customer service at 1-800-331-4331. The recall number is 26TA17.

Other than saying the EV-ECU is being reprogrammed, Toyota has not yet announced next steps for owners of affected vehicles outside North America. The KBA reference number is 17116R.

Check back for more details. The recall only affects the 2026 C-HR. The 2027 Toyota C-HR is also now on sale.

#4548. Ford Just Started Fathom LFP Battery Production In Michigan. It's A Big Deal

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Ford just reached a critical milestone in the development of its Fathom electric truck. The company has started manufacturing low-cost lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) battery packs at its $3 billion BlueOval Battery Park Michigan, located a couple hours west of Detroit, in Marshall, MI. These are production-grade LFP batteries which will first be used in Fathom prototypes before full-scale manufacturing begins next year.

One can’t overstate how important the Marshall plant is for Ford. It’s the first plant in the U.S. to manufacture LFP batteries for mainstream consumer vehicle use domestically. LG Energy Solution also produces LFP batteries in the U.S.—supplying to GM and Tesla—but they’re dedicated to stationary energy storage systems. Ford’s 2 million-square-foot facility is dedicated to automotive LFP batteries.

It has an annual production capacity of 20 gigawatt-hours and can manufacture 50 battery packs every hour. It’s a vertically integrated plant, where materials like raw lithium and iron-phosphate powder go in one end, and fully assembled, ready-to-install battery packs come out the other. All anode and cathode production, as well as major production processes in between, happen inside the plant.

Alan Clarke, the vice president of advanced development projects at Ford, said the company is moving fast to bring the Fathom to the market. In a relatively short time period, he claimed, Ford had developed the all-new Universal EV Platform that will underpin its future EVs, an all-new production system at the Louisville Assembly Plant, and domestic LFP battery production.

“Not having a team that existed to have a battery factory, a unicasting factory, an entirely new most automated vehicle production facility that Ford's ever produced in less than five years would be I think faster than China speed,” Clarke said during a media roundtable at the BlueOval Battery Park Michigan on Tuesday.

Clarke previously worked at Tesla for 12 years, helping create the Model S, followed by development work for the Model X, Model Y, Model 3, and Cybertruck.

BlueOval Battery Park Michigan drone photo

I toured Ford’s LFP plant this week, and I think it’s one of the most advanced, highly-automated battery facilities in the U.S. Michigan, America’s automotive manufacturing hub for a century, certainly hasn’t seen anything like it in its history.

Part of the reason why the facility is so cutting-edge comes from Ford’s LFP licensing deal with China’s CATL, the world’s largest and the most advanced battery maker. The U.S. has been lagging behind China and Europe in the battery technology race. Ford is now bringing that technical know-how back to the U.S. even if that means licensing technology from CATL.

More importantly, Ford officials said the new plant is fully compliant with the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) rules. Raw materials used to make batteries here do not come from what the U.S. government designates as Foreign Entities of Concern (FEOC). Even though the technology is from CATL, the critical materials aren’t sourced from U.S. FEOCs such as China, Russia and North Korea. (China controls the vast majority of the global critical materials supply chain.)

Final inspection of the Ford Fathom's LFP prismatic cells.

The plant is fully owned and operated by Ford, but CATL engineers helped the company set up thousands of incredibly complex production tools. They’re also helping train workers to operate high-tech equipment and install tight quality control systems to help Ford deliver the affordable EV that it has long promised. The prismatic LFP cell itself is unique to Ford and not something that exists in CATL’s global portfolio.

Meng Wang, the director and chief engineer of battery cell industrialization at Ford summed up the CATL partnership well. “To shorten our time to market, we decided to learn from the best,” Wang said. “Throughout the process, CATL passed on critical knowledge to Ford, including the equipment functions, manufacturing process, and also quality controls.”

Preorders for the Ford Fathom will begin early 2027 and production and deliveries are expected to begin by the end of next year.

#4546. The 2027 Hyundai Elantra Is Bigger and Much, Much Bolder

A sharp-edged “Art of Steel” design gives the Korean compact unmistakable panache.

The Hyundai Elantra continues to defy the apparent incipient death of the sedan, and the Korean automaker just gave it a major upgrade for 2027. Between a new “Art of Steel” design, a larger size, and upgraded infotainment technology, the 2027 Hyundai Elantra is more prepared for the future than ever before.

Revealed Thursday at the 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show, the 2027 Elantra's most obvious feature is its exterior design. Created under Hyundai's new Art of Steel design philosophy, which was first revealed on the Boulder concept, the Elantra is now a boxy beast with wide fenders, sharp headlights, and a square rear end. This new sedan was designed with a very clear three-box configuration and sport sedan dynamism in mind, according to Hyundai’s head of design.

“There is an inherent beauty in a sedan because its proportions are honest, intuitive and functional,” said SangYup Lee, executive vice president and head of the Hyundai and Genesis Global Design Center. “With the all-new Elantra, we returned to that essence, then pushed it forward. Wide, muscular fenders, a long hood, and refined three-box proportions give Elantra a confident, athletic presence that challenges the conventions of the compact sedan.”

In addition to the new exterior design, changes under the skin mean the latest Elantra is now 3.3 inches longer, 1.1 inches wider, and features a 1.1-inch longer wheelbase than its predecessor; all told, Hyundai says the 2027 Elantra has over one inch more rear headroom and legroom. So-called H-Edge lighting, futuristic grille styling, slim- neck mirrors, and lift-up flush door handles make up the rest of the visual changes.

But Hyundai didn’t stop its design renovations with the exterior. Inside the Elantra, the carmaker added a new Curve of Upholstery design and an asymmetrical front layout, which is meant to “gently embrace” the driver. A central 12.9-inch Pleos Connect infotainment system is standard on all Elantra models, while an available slim information display in the driver’s natural line of sight provides critical driving information. Other interior features include 15-kW dual wireless phone charging, Audio by Bang & Olufsen, Hyundai Digital Key 2, and 100-watt ultra-fast charging USB ports. Upholstery will be available in four black color combinations, as well as Burgundy/Rose Ivory and Chalk Beige.

Mechanically, the Elantra is a bit less exciting. The new model will offer two powertrain options: a 1.6-liter hybrid four-cylinder powerplant, and a naturally-aspirated 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine. The hybrid model will deliver 154 horsepower through a six-speed dual-clutch transmission, while the purely internal combustion model offers 146 horsepower routed through a continuously variable transmission. Hybridized Elantra models also feature a predictive drive system that intelligently anticipates driving patterns and road conditions to maximize efficiency, as well as a new “Stay Mode” that lets the climate control, stereo, charging ports and other non-motion-related functions operate for up to 30 minutes with the engine off.

The pure ICE version will arrive as a 2027 model year Elantra, while the new Hyundai Elantra Hybrid will debut as a 2028 model year vehicle. Specific on-sale timing, pricing, fuel economy ratings and other details will be revealed closer to the vehicle’s American launch.

#4545. US battery storage just topped 200 GWh – here’s where it is

The US has installed more than 200 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of battery storage, with nearly 50 GWh coming online in the first nine months of 2026 alone.

The US added 48.3 GWh of battery storage through September, up 20% from the same stretch last year, according to the latest report from the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA) and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence. Q3 was a little slower: The US installed 14.3 GWh in those three months, down 1% year over year.

Texas added 12.3 GWh of grid-scale batteries through September, more than any other state. Arizona came in second at 7.7 GWh, followed by California at 6.8 GWh. And 11 states had already broken their annual storage installation records with three months to go – Colorado, Massachusetts, Utah, Michigan, Georgia, Mississippi, Virginia, Iowa, Montana, Alabama, and Illinois.

Utility-scale batteries did most of the work in Q3, accounting for 12.2 GWh of new capacity. Businesses and industrial sites added another 1.3 GWh, and residential added 746 megawatt-hours (MWh). That was the best Q3 yet for home batteries, though installs through September were still down 12% year over year. Some homeowners moved up their installations last year before the federal residential clean energy tax credit ended.

“States are moving from targets to centralized procurements,” said Pete Tillotson, a senior analyst at Benchmark. In September, New York awarded contracts for eight battery projects that can deliver about 950 megawatts (MW) combined. SEIA and Benchmark now expect 708 GWh of storage across the grid, homes, and businesses by 2030, up 3.7% from their previous forecast.

The US can also make more battery cells here. A Tennessee factory opened in July and an Indiana factory opened in October, bringing US cell manufacturing capacity to 92.4 GWh, up 50%.

Solar and batteries helped bring down average summer wholesale power prices by 42% in Texas’s ERCOT market and 51% in California’s CAISO market between 2021 and 2026, according to SEIA’s inflation-adjusted analysis. When batteries had power to spare during peak hours, grid operators could call on expensive power plants less often.

You wouldn’t know it from looking at the total on residential electric bills. The cost of generating power for households fell in both markets, but the cost of delivering it to homes rose. Overall, residential bills rose 22% at the two California utilities SEIA examined and 3% across its Texas utility sample, driven by higher transmission and distribution costs. California is upgrading its grid to reduce the risk of wildfires. Texas is expanding its grid for rising demand and make it more resilient to storms.

The article is good with the reporting about grid tied storage, but seems to miss the forest for the trees with it comes to pricing. Texas isn't installing more grid tied storage because of altruistic intent.

The storage is being added because they electricity suppliers can use it to make money. They can make money because we have a reasonably well thought out wholesale electrical market AND because that market has purchases large amounts of solar and wind generation.

That combination means that I still pay just $0.01 more per kwh than I did when I moved to this state 20 years ago. I pay 12 cents per kwh and Texas average is between 12 and 15. A functional market is what makes that work.

More than 300 solar and battery storage companies in the US wrote to Congress last week asking it to pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act. SEIA CEO Tim Pawlenty says the permitting bill would help get projects built faster and ease pressure on power prices. However, many Democrats feel this bill falls short. The Senate voted 70–27 on Monday to end debate on the amendment containing the bill’s text, moving it closer to a final vote.

#4544. Kia Made Its First EV 40 Years Ago. It Shows How Far Electric Cars Have Come

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Kia has cemented itself as one of the world’s premier electric vehicle manufacturers. And it's spent longer experimenting with EVs than you probably think. This week, Kia marked 40 years since its first EV hit the road. It shows just how far the automaker—and the EV industry—has come.

Kia’s first EV launched in 1986 and was very important for several reasons. It was based on a van called the Besta. This was Kia’s first van developed in-house, replacing the Mazda-based Bongo van that it was making before.

Ahead of the 1986 Asian Games, Kia decided to develop a marathon broadcast vehicle that could keep pace with runners and house timekeeping and camera equipment—all while not disturbing runners with exhaust fumes. So the automaker ripped out the Besta's 2.0-liter diesel engine and replaced it with an electric motor and 35 kilowatt-hours worth of lead-acid batteries.

The range wasn’t great, but it was enough to cover the whole 26.2-mile marathon on one charge. Hyundai says it had around 75 miles of range and a top speed of 56 mph. It made another appearance at the 1998 Seoul Olympics.

Most importantly, Kia says the Besta EV was South Korea’s first-ever EV. The brand would go on to continue developing EV prototypes like the 1991 Sonata EV and 1992 Excel. In 1993, the Pride EV hatchback became Korea’s first EV certified for commercial sale, although it didn't get a full production run. This car, which you may have known in gas form as the Ford Festiva, had an (estimated) 17.4 kWh battery and solar panels that Kia said were good for almost ten miles of additional range.

The Kia Ray was the brand's first production electric vehicle, launching in 2011 with 86 miles of range.

Eventually, Kia made its first true production model, the Ray EV, in 2011. It had a 16.4 kWh battery pack and 86 miles of range. Three years later in 2014, the Soul EV came to market, bringing a Kia EV to the U.S. for the first time. And things really took off from there.

There’s only a four-year gap between the 93-mile Soul EV and the 238-mile Niro EV. In a relatively short amount of time, Kia’s EVs went from being useful as a second car to having enough range to be a sole vehicle. Today the company has a deep and competitive line of EV models, including the EV2, EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6 and EV9—although we are missing some of those options in the U.S.

And forty years after the Besta, Kia is back to making electric vans. The PV5 went on sale last year, offering several battery options and a range of up to 258 miles WLTP. Sales are off to a promising start; Kia says it sold some 57,000 of them in the van's first 14 months on the market.

#4543. Fiona the hippo dies at age 9

Published Nov 19, 2026 4:25 PM EST

The Cincinnati Zoo’s most famous resident Fiona the hippo has died at age 9.

“We are in shock at the moment,” Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike said in a statement. “We did not expect this outcome. She fought until she couldn’t anymore. Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn’t fight anymore. She was dearly loved by her Zoo family and countless others around the world. Her loss will be felt deeply by so many.”

Last week, a child’s knit hat entered her enclosure at the Cincinnati Zoo and the almost 10-year-old hippo ate it. Given her size, zookeepers initially thought she’d simply pass the hat, but it remained stuck in her digestive track. She had undergone a colonoscopy using a 9-foot scope and multiple ultrasounds that showed intestinal bunching, indicating her body was trying and expel the hat. Caretakers have continued to give her fluids and sedate her when necessary for tests. Just yesterday, on November 18, the zoo shared a new approach in Fiona’s ongoing treatment: a vibration plate borrowed from a local Ohio horse farm. Fiona could be seen standing on the plate, vocalizing to caretakers.

“Fiona was such a gift,” said Cincinnati Zoo Executive Chair of the Board Thane Maynard. “I have never known an animal so beloved in all my life. From the day she was born, she was like lightning in a bottle. And, she will be remembered and beloved many years from now.”

Fiona first captured the internet’s heart in 2017, when she was born six weeks premature. Baby hippos typically weigh about 100 pounds at birth, but tiny Fiona tipped the scales at a mere 29 pounds. She was the smallest known hippo to survive such a low birth weight. As she grew, Fiona took social media and the real world by storm: she photobombed an engagement shoot, had a local ice cream named in her honor, and even starred in her own reality-TV series appropriately called “The Fiona Show.”  Her surprise baby brother Fritz was born in 2022, after their mother’s birth control went “on the fritz.”

#4542. Toyota’s Corolla Cross Deck Is a Forbidden Fruit Rival To the Ford Maverick

The four-door unibody pickup, unfortunately, seems only destined for Latin America and the Caribbean for the moment.

Toyota has had incredible success with pickup trucks in the United States of America. The Tacoma has become one of America’s perennial best-selling vehicles, while the Tundra has carved out a sustainable niche in America’s grueling full-size segment. But there’s arguably room for more.

Rumors have long suggested Toyota is working on a compact, Ford Maverick-fighting pickup that would fill the truck lineup’s glaring need for a cheaper and more efficient option. Dealers have reportedly been asking Toyota for a compact pickup for several years. Mark Templin, Toyota’s COO in the United States, confirmed Toyota is “looking at” bringing a smaller pickup to the U.S. back in May 2025. And now, Toyota has just unveiled a new pickup that could fit that bill … for Latin American and Caribbean markets.

Toyota revealed a new compact pickup called the Corolla Cross Deck on Wednesday during its inauguration of a new production facility in Sococaba, Brazil, and it will enter production in the first half of 2027. According to Motor1 Brazil, the Corolla Cross Deck shares a TNGA-C platform with the Corolla sedan and Corolla Cross SUV. Toyota did not provide full specs, but did reveal a hybrid version—likely featuring the 1.8-liter 122-horsepower powertrain Toyota uses for the Corolla Cross in that market.

Sadly, Toyota has not confirmed potential availability for the Corolla Cross Deck in the American market. The automaker did not respond to a Road & Track inquiry about its potential availability by the time of publication, but we’ll update this story if we receive a response.

On paper, a Corolla-based compact pickup would likely be the easiest route for Toyota to bring a small, cheap pickup to the United States in the foreseeable future. Toyota already builds the Corolla and Corolla Cross at its Mazda Toyota Manufacturing Facility in Alabama; a new truck truck could be built on the same line—and even spawn potential rebadged variants for Toyota partners Mazda and Subaru.

In the American market, the Toyota Corolla Cross uses 2.0-liter gas and hybrid engines. That powertrain could give Toyota options for a 169-horsepower base gas model truck—potentially starting below $30,000—and a 196-hp hybrid version that could eclipse 40 miles per gallon.

That said, one could also see Toyota needing a different small truck approach to resonate with an American audience. One of Ford’s great innovations with the Maverick was that it looks more like the F-150 and Ranger than the Escape crossover it shared a platform with. And even if a new Toyota pickup were to share its bones with the Corolla, Toyota may want to brand it as an extension of the pickup line, rather than the Corolla family.

#4541. The BMW i3 Has The Nurburgring Skills To Match Its Impressive Range

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Who needs the electric M3 when the regular BMW i3 can already dominate at the track? In this new video from Misha Charoudin, the BMW i3 50 takes to the Nurburgring and not only makes it around the Green Hell without issue, it actually beats up on other performance cars.

The BMW i3 50 xDrive is currently the only variant on sale, and while it isn't a full-blown M car, it has the specs to rival most of the real ones. Its dual motors combine for 463 horsepower and 476 lb-ft of torque, making it more powerful than most M3s throughout history. Those motors get fed electrons by a 109 kWh battery, which is far bigger than most electric sedans of its size. Such a big battery might seem like overkill in an i3, especially since its heft might not seem useful on track. However, that massive pack actually helped it at the 'Ring.

When Charoudin started the lap, he had 79% state-of-charge (SoC). When he finished the 12-mile lap as hard as he could, he had 65%. A 14% drop after pushing the i3 hard on the most difficult track in the world is pretty dang good. Even more impressive is that, after three more laps with someone else at the helm, it still had 20% battery. Depending on where that i3 calls home, it could have been driven back after four flat-out laps. That's pretty remarkable, especially considering this is just the normal i3.

What's most impressive, though, is how the i3 50 handled the Nurburgring itself. On a normal day, the 'Ring is clogged up by countless sports cars, and even boring rental cars, so unless you're properly quick, you can get caught behind a train of cars. But not the i3. It carved through the traffic with ease, overtook even some serious performance machines, and looked like the fastest car on the track at times.

During the lap, you can see its sharp turn in, explosive power, and strong braking, both regenerative and friction. What's more, it did all of that on eco-friendly EV tires in the cold. So imagine what one could do on a set of stickier summer tires in good temps. The battery didn't even overheat, with the temp gauge saying "OK" until the very last minute. It did eventually say the battery temps got high, but the lap was basically done by that point.

This is the same BMW i3 50 that gets 468 miles of EPA-rated range and drove from Norway to Spain while only charging for a total of two hours and 46 minutes. If it can smoke performance cars at the Nurburgring, can you imagine what the M3 will be like?

#4538. Waymo Suspends Freeway Operations Across U.S. After California Ban

The autonomous vehicle operator’s halt is temporary, but freeway testing will continue with specialists behind the wheel.

A week after Waymo was banned from operating on California freeways, the autonomous rideshare service has now paused freeway operations across the United States.

The California-based startup announced the temporary pause on Wednesday, November 18, although it actually began on November 11. Normally, Waymo offers freeway service in the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Miami, and Austin. The Associated Press cited a Waymo statement saying it is temporarily restricting “commercial freeway rides in all markets where we operate that service.” However, Waymo said it would continue freeway testing with trained autonomous specialists at the wheel.

It is not immediately clear when the freeway pause will be lifted. California initiated the ban last week after multiple incidents of Waymo vehicles driving into construction zones or disobeying orders from law enforcement; the state DMV said an incident on November 5 and another on November 6 drove the regulatory agency to ban autonomous freeway operations.

“The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present,” California DMV spokesperson Jonathan Groveman said to the Associated Press. “The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present.”

Road & Track has reached out to Waymo for comment, and will update the story if we learn more.

#4537. A Tesla Model Y Without A Steering Wheel Is Coming: Musk

Browse this and many other websites without banner ads, personalized tracking and video ads.

Tesla has already built one model without a steering wheel or pedals. But one was not enough, and CEO Elon Musk is eyeing another model for an autonomous upgrade.

Musk said Wednesday that Tesla will build a steering-wheel-free, fully autonomous version of the Model Y.

Musk revealed the plan at the New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, noting that Tesla wants to take the basic premise of what it can offer with the Cybercab—a fully autonomous vehicle that can operate as a managed fleet car—to a platform that can seat more than just two people.

"It's going to make sense for us to make cars that can seat different amounts of people,” said Musk. “We still need autonomous vehicles if you've got four or six, or a whole family. What we plan to do is have an autonomous version of the Model Y that won't have steering wheels or pedals and would be good for transporting groups of six or seven people."

Now, before getting too far—yes, you’re still going to be able to order a regular-size Model Y with a steering wheel for the foreseeable future. But Tesla wants a robotaxi that can accommodate an actual family.

Tesla already uses the Model Y in its autonomous fleet. However, those cars retain the basic driving controls that Tesla now wants to eliminate in its fully autonomous variant. Musk’s proposed version would seemingly delete them from the factory and create a larger autonomous car that passengers could ride in, but not drive—similar to the Cybercab.

To Musk’s point, Cybercab is intentionally tiny. Its two-seat configuration “covers 90% of all passenger miles,” according to Musk. That means that Tesla can cut down on production costs by reducing the interior complexity in order to make the Cybercab cost under $30,000.

Musk didn’t say when (or if) this variant would be offered to the public to purchase. The Cybercab only recently became available for hand-picked private buyers to purchase, and even then, there are a number of asterisks involved (like where the car can operate, and the mandatory $300 per month autonomy subscription required for the car to move).

Nevertheless, if Tesla is going to build driverless cars, an autonomous Model Y makes sense if Tesla can keep costs down and safely deploy it in enough usable areas. But with a $300 per month cost on top of the vehicle, would Tesla’s ideal audience be fleet operators or private buyers?

#4536. Lego’s New Formula 1 Speed Champions Collection Includes Tiny Versions of All 22 Current F1 Drivers

Our car experts choose every product we feature. We may earn money from the links on this page.

The helmets, race suits, and even hair have been custom-designed to be as true-to-life as possible. (For a minifig, at least.)

It’s been two years since Lego and Formula 1 first partnered up to translate the excitement of the grand prix grid into tiny, plastic, painful-to-step-on brick form. But while the race cars were a realistic low-polygon tribute to the life-size real things, the minifigures that accompanied them were fairly generic. Until now, that is, because the upcoming Lego Speed Champions lineup features all 11 teams on the 2026 grid and all 22 full-time drivers, rendered with realistic driving suits and customized hair.

Announced at the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix against a backdrop of several giant minifigures and a full complement of Lego-clad go-karts (now updated with neon LED light strips for the full Vegas experience), this next batch of Speed Champions sets will go on sale March 1, 2027. That makes for plenty of time to build all 11 before the first race of the season in Bahrain, although it’s also yet another thing to wait for during the off-season.

Arvid Lindblad, driver for the Visa Cash App Racing Bulls Team, made at appearance at Lego’s press announcement, and posed with both his large and small Lego likenesses. Asked about his thoughts on the result, the British driver said: “Awesome, nailed it. They got the hair perfect,” adding that, “I’ve always loved Legos, though I never imagined having my own minifigure.”

And speaking of hair, yes, the Valteri Bottas minifigure is rocking a mullet. Each plastic hairpiece was approved by the respective drivers. “When we pitched the the hairstyles to the teams and the drivers, they absolutely loved it,” said Will Thorogood, the Lego designer who led this effort. “They all thought it was as funny as we did.”

Another key part of bringing out the driver’s personality is the helmets, which are “far more detailed than any helmet we've ever done before with the with the Lego production,” according to Thorogood. Lando Norris’s helmet, for example, “has all the blob details on it” as well as a minifigure Easter egg hidden in the design. Each driver also comes with two facial expressions on opposite sides of the minfigure head; Charles Leclerc’s visage is either relaxed in sunglasses or a more serious grimace, both with the Ferrari driver’s stubbled mustache and goatee.

The cars themselves reflect the new regulations and, says Thorogood, “as you look closely, you'll see every single one is built completely differently to capture all the aero details and principles that each of the teams has employed.” These too feature several Easter eggs for Lego fans, such as suspension wishbones made from wizard wands and rear diffuser strakes made from minifigure meat cleavers.

Measuring 7.5 inches long and 2.5 inches wide, the Speed Champions sets will be priced at $29.99 when they go on sale next year. More photos and details are viewable now on the Speed Champions section of the Lego Website.
